status_summary: Executive Order 14149 (signed 2025-01-20) bars federal departments and personnel from using federal resources contrary to its free-speech policy and directs the Attorney General to investigate the prior four years of federal activity and report to the President with remedial recommendations, with no deadline; no report under that order was found. On 2025-02-05 Attorney General Bondi issued a memo that rescinds the October 2021 Garland memo on school board meetings and creates a Weaponization Working Group; on 2026-10-05 that group released a report on the Garland memo (which cites Executive Order 14147 and, in the text reviewed, not 14149) announcing remedies for affected parents. The FTC opened a request for information on technology platform censorship on 2025-02-20 (comments due 2025-05-21) and, on 2025-09-26, issued a final consent order barring Omnicom from steering advertising on the basis of publishers' political or ideological viewpoints, news-accuracy views or diversity commitments, except at an advertiser's express direction. A separate FTC civil investigative demand to Media Matters drew a First Amendment preliminary injunction (2025-08-15); the FTC withdrew the demand on 2026-04-16 and the D.C. Circuit dismissed the FTC's appeal on 2026-05-04 on the parties' joint stipulation. No federal measure aimed at the campus-speech or donor-harassment examples in the Foreword was found.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14149 (published 2025-01-28), which bars federal resources from being used contrary to its free-speech policy and directs the Attorney General to investigate federal activity over the prior four years and report with remedial recommendations. The order sets no deadline and creates no enforceable rights.

Attorney General Pamela Bondi issues a memo titled Restoring the Integrity and Credibility of the Department of Justice. A footnote rescinds Attorney General Garland's October 4, 2021 memo on parents at local government meetings, and the memo creates a Weaponization Working Group to review enforcement activity of the prior four years.

FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson announces a public inquiry and request for information on how technology platforms deny or degrade users' access based on their speech or affiliations; comments were due 2025-05-21.

FTC publishes a proposed consent order with Omnicom and Interpublic that bars steering ad spending toward or away from publishers because of political or ideological viewpoints, with comments due 2025-07-28.

Attorney General Bondi sends a memo to the FBI Director and U.S. Attorneys on protecting parents' First Amendment rights in education and responding to credible threats against parents; the press release does not mention the Garland memo or the Working Group.

FTC issues the final Omnicom and IPG Decision and Order (Docket C-4823; Commissioner Meador recused). It bars agreements and exclusion lists that direct ad spending based on publishers' political or ideological viewpoints (including views on news accuracy), adherence to third-party journalistic standards, or diversity commitments, except at a client's express direction, and provides for a monitor who receives nonparty complaints.

The FTC moves in the D.C. Circuit to dismiss its appeal of the 2025-08-15 preliminary injunction in Media Matters for America v. FTC, saying staff withdrew the May 2025 civil investigative demand on 2026-04-16 after an antitrust settlement in FTC v. Dentsu. Media Matters opposed the motion.
